B: Hi! Oh, hello, can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah, loud and clear. Hiya. I'm Rob.
B: Oh, ha, my husband's called Rob. Sorry, that's going to throw me now. I'm Gemma.
A: I'll try not to take it personally.
B: No, it's a good name! Erm, how did you find the puzzle bit?
A: Fine, I think. I sort of panicked on the last couple and just guessed, if I'm honest.
B: Same, yeah. I'm not a puzzle person really, I'm more, you know, hands-on. So what do you do?
A: I'm a student, actually. Mature student. Second year of an ecology degree at Man Met. I was in council admin for about eight years before that and got bored, so, yeah, packed it in and went back.
B: Oh, that's brilliant. That's quite brave, isn't it?
A: Erm, maybe. Bit skint, mostly. But I'm enjoying it. I do bat surveys in the summer as well, for a consultancy, which is the fun bit. Standing in a field at eleven at night with a detector.
B: That sounds amazing, actually. I saw the binoculars in your picture and thought, birdwatcher.
A: Guilty. And the cat's tail. That's Moss.
B: I did see the tail! We've got a greyhound, Pip. She basically lives on the sofa.
A: Rescue?
B: Yeah, rescue. She's lovely, but she refuses to go out in the rain. She just plants her feet at the door and looks at me like, absolutely not.
A: Fair enough, to be honest. So what about you, what do you do?
B: I'm an upholsterer. Self-employed, sort of part-time. I've got a little unit on a trading estate in Didcot and I do dining chairs, footstools, the odd armchair. I love it, honestly, the best bit is when you strip an old chair back and find, like, horsehair stuffing, or someone's really dodgy repair from the seventies with drawing pins in it. It's like being a detective.
A: That's cool, actually. Is that something you trained in, or?
B: Did a City and Guilds course in my early thirties, and then I worked with an older upholsterer for a bit before he retired. Before that it was retail and admin, so, kind of like you, I suppose. Bit of a late swap.
A: Yeah, the admin escape club.
B: Ha, yes! Do you think you'll stay up north after, or?
A: Hopefully, yeah. My partner Hannah's a dental nurse in Stockport, so I'd like to get a job with a wildlife trust round here. Field ecologist, ideally. Something outdoors, anyway.
B: Oh, that'd be lovely. Do you walk a lot then? You've got a map up as well.
A: Yeah, Dark Peak. I'm out there most weekends I can be. It's sort of what kept me sane in the office job, really.
B: I get that. I do walks round the lakes with Pip in the morning, and parkrun every now and then. Not fast, though.
A: Nobody's fast at parkrun except the ten people at the front.
B: Exactly! I'm firmly with the buggies at the back. Erm, do you do any other sport?
A: Bouldering, a bit. At a wall in town. I'm sort of middling. There's a lot of nineteen-year-olds who make it look easy, which is annoying.
B: Oh, I'd be terrible at that. I'd just hang there.
A: That's most of it, honestly. Hanging there, thinking.
B: Ha. Do you take photos as well, with the birds?
A: Yeah, I've got a secondhand camera. I don't post them much though. I saw a barn owl on a field trip last term and got one decent shot, so I'm quite made up with that.
